intended_object: Given a supernatural (Steinitz) exponent family e : primes → ℕ ∪ {∞}, this is the product ∏_{p : 0<e_p<∞} ℤ/p^{e_p} × ∏_{p : e_p=∞} ℤ_p, with the trivial factors at e_p = 0 left out. It is the standard model of the procyclic group of order e (≅ Ẑ/eẐ), as in Neukirch–Schmidt–Wingberg I §7. Source: the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The body is exactly the product described. The first factor is a dependent product over the primes p with 0 < e p < ⊤ of ZMod (p^(e p).toNat). On that index set the exponent is finite, so `toNat` gives the actual exponent. The second factor is a dependent product over the primes with e p = ⊤ of ℤ_[p]. Both index sets may be infinite, which is right: a procyclic group can have infinitely many nontrivial primary parts.

The `ULift.{u}` wrappers only move the type to universe u and do not change the mathematics. Because the definition is an `abbrev`, the product group and topology structures come from instance inference. These are the product topology, the discrete topology on ZMod and the p-adic topology on ℤ_p, which is the intended profinite structure.

Leaving out the e_p = 0 factors is harmless, since those factors are ZMod 1, the trivial group. The library shows this in `primewisePadicQuotientModelContinuousAddEquivSupportProduct`, which builds a continuous additive isomorphism from the full all-primes quotient model.

The setting is not too narrow, because the construction is specifically indexed by primes and supernatural exponents. Mathlib has no notion of supernatural numbers and no product of this shape, so there is no Mathlib counterpart.
